submitter: bugfix_475_delivery_email_instructions lane (session '475'). The MECHANISM half of bugs_open/475, split by agreement with the site_delivery_and_editor lane who hold the COPY half. The OTHER CONSUMER of the seam being changed is the bugs_open/477 lane, who own send_followup_email_action.go; they have been told before this submission, have converged on the placeholder name, and have asked to object in-round. OWNER RULING 2026-07-29 s3 (a shared mechanism's other consumers must be TOLD, not merely measured) is discharged.
rationale:
WHAT IS WRONG, AND IT IS NOT THE SENTENCE.

bugs_open/475 is a FALSE STATEMENT TO A PAYING CUSTOMER. delivery-email-sender's live
body_template says "The ZIP comes with instructions that walk you through putting it on free
hosting." The ZIP contains 45 site files and no document of any kind. [MEASURED 2026-09-04 14:40Z]
at the live agent_definitions row - timestamped deliberately, because migration 776 was applied to
that SAME jsonb path at 12:05:25Z the same day for an unrelated false-promise clause, so "that
template was migrated today" is not evidence either way. The bugs_open/477 lane independently
confirmed the clause with a LIKE predicate. Two lanes, two instruments, same answer.

The point fix is obvious and I am NOT proposing it: add {{instructions_link}} to fillTemplate and a
fifth line to each of the two guard slices. I am not proposing it because it GROWS the structure
that is the actual defect.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: TWO CUSTOMER LETTERS, ONE VOCABULARY, TWO HAND-KEPT MIRRORS.

send_delivery_email_action.go fills its template through fillTemplate (:197-206), a
strings.NewReplacer over a CLOSED vocabulary of seven tokens. It guards with a hand-written slice
(:125-134) that must run BEFORE delivery.Claim stamps the handover - because a named token with no
value is replaced by an EMPTY STRING, so the customer reads "Your files: " with nothing after it,
and NO POST-FILL SCAN CAN SEE THAT, because the fill succeeded. The post-fill "{{" backstop
(:168-175) fires AFTER the stamp, which is worse.

send_followup_email_action.go - a SECOND customer letter, built by the 477 lane, seeded disabled by
migration 775 - CALLS THE SAME fillTemplate (:224) and keeps its OWN MIRRORED guard slice
(:166-172).

The contract holding those two lists in step is A COMMENT, in that file, at :150-164:

  "The only other placeholder-refusal in the estate is send_delivery_email's, which this copies
   deliberately rather than shares. ... If a shared mechanism is ever built, these two are its
   first two callers."
  "If fillTemplate's vocabulary grows, this list must grow with it."

OWNER RULING 2026-08-02 s2 (RFC_010) already ruled on exactly this shape: "A comment is not a
control on a tree this many sessions share."

AND THE ESTATE DEMONSTRATED IT THIS AFTERNOON, LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICALLY. Two sessions, both
careful, both correct, independently chose TWO NAMES FOR ONE CONCEPT for the new instructions
placeholder: this lane's {{instructions_link}} and the 477 lane's {{instructions_url}}. What caught
it was one lane having written that comment and the other thinking to send a cross-session message.
NEITHER IS A MECHANISM. Half a day's difference in timing and the estate would carry two
differently-named placeholders for one page, filled by two different mechanisms, in two letters to
the same customer.

WHAT THIS CHANGE DOES.

Single-source the vocabulary and DERIVE both guards from it, so "the filler knows a token the guard
does not" becomes UNREPRESENTABLE rather than discouraged. A sender declares an Availability for
every token; Fill.Check refuses on COVERAGE (a token nobody declared) before it refuses on
AVAILABILITY (a token the template names with no value). Coverage is checked unconditionally, not
only when a template happens to name the token, so adding a token to the Vocabulary makes every
sender that has not been taught refuse LOUDLY and PRE-STAMP - recoverable - instead of mailing an
empty string. {{instructions_link}} then lands as the first single-sourced entry rather than the
last hand-copied one.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, stated so no seat has to ask.

It checks PLACEHOLDERS. It cannot check PROSE. "The ZIP comes with instructions" carries no
placeholder and was invisible to the existing guard; it will be invisible to this one. The change
NARROWS the class by making the customer-facing artefact a link, and links are checked. It does not
eliminate it. A generic "false English claim" detector was considered and rejected (see edit 5's
rationale).

WHY THIS IS COUNCIL-SCOPE AND NOT AN RFC. Under OWNER RULING 2026-07-29 s1, a shared-vocabulary
addition needs an RFC only when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES. This one
STRENGTHENS the guarantee (from "a comment asks you to keep two lists in step" to "an undeclared
token refuses before the stamp") and adds NO new authority - so RFC_022's narrowing does not bite
either: there is no new opt-in field whose unsafe default is OFF. If the architecture seat reads it
otherwise I would rather hear that now.

ORDERING, WHICH IS A LIVE FAILURE MODE AND NOT A PREFERENCE. Config is live on apply; Go is inert
until a roll. A template naming {{instructions_link}} before the binary knows it leaves the literal
in the body, trips the post-fill "{{" scan - and that scan fires AFTER the handover is stamped. The
result is a stamped, undeliverable handover needing the operator re-mint recipe. So NO MIGRATION IS
IN THIS ROUND. The template change comes only after this code has rolled, verified by
service_binary_capabilities plus git merge-base --is-ancestor.

The owner has separately ruled NO interim copy change ("leave it") until the instructions page
exists, so there is no competing change queued against that jsonb path.

plan.summary: Single-source the delivery-letter placeholder vocabulary and DERIVE both senders' pre-claim guards from it, so a token cannot exist in the filler and be missing from a guard. Land {{instructions_link}} (bugs_open/475) as its first single-sourced entry. Two callers, one new file, one shared test helper, no schema change, NO MIGRATION in this round.

edits.symbol: Token, Vocabulary, Availability, Fill, Fill.Check, Fill.Apply
edits.rationale: The single source. Today the token set lives in fillTemplate's strings.NewReplacer and its 'must be produced' rule lives in two hand-copied slices in two files. Making them one structure is what turns the drift from discouraged into unrepresentable. Fill.Check refuses on COVERAGE first (an undeclared token) and AVAILABILITY second (a declared-but-empty one), both PRE-CLAIM, which is the only place a refusal is free. NOTE the type is named Token, not Link: the seven members have three provenances and {{days}} is not a link at all - it is AdvertisedWindowDays, a constant deliberately set to 30 while LiveLinkWindow serves 42. A link-shaped table would have silently dropped the one entry whose correct value is not the obvious one. That correction came from the 477 lane before any code was written.

Delete the hand-written guard slice and the private closed vocabulary; build a delivery.Fill and call Check pre-claim / Apply post-claim. Behaviour is preserved exactly for the four tokens guarded today. The post-fill '{{' scan STAYS - it is the backstop for a template naming something outside the vocabulary entirely, and this change does not make it redundant.

edits.symbol: the :166-172 mirrored guard slice, the {{instructions_url}} pre-substitution at :224-225
edits.rationale: The second caller, and the reason this is a framework change. Its mirrored slice goes; its {{instructions_url}} strings.ReplaceAll pre-substitution goes with it, converging both letters on ONE name. CRITICAL: its {{zip_link}} case must survive as NeverReason, NOT as an empty Value. The 477 lane's intent is 'this caller can never produce this one, at any time, BY CONSTRUCTION - a scheduled follow-up has no zip step and no presign to mint'. Flattening it to 'empty => refuse' behaves identically today and LOSES THE REASON, and the reason is the only thing that stops a later session 'fixing' it by wiring a presign into the scheduled follow-up. This file is the 477 lane's; they have seen this submission and asked to object in-round.

The control that makes drift fail in CI rather than in an inbox. A shared helper both senders' tests call, asserting a Fill covers the Vocabulary exactly - omission AND invention. Plus assertions on the refusal TEXT, because a receipt nobody asserts on is a log line. THE MUTATION CHECK IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE, not a nicety: add a Token to Vocabulary, do NOT teach the senders, and prove both suites go red and both Check calls refuse. Without mutating, a passing test cannot distinguish 'the guard works' from 'something else in series refused first'.

edits.symbol: Links, LinkConfig, the links literal in Claim
edits.rationale: Carry the instructions URL: Links.Instructions + LinkConfig.InstructionsURL, populated in Claim's links literal. It is a PLAIN DURABLE URL with no token and no lifetime - a hard constraint from the 477 lane, not a preference: their scheduled follow-up refuses any placeholder it cannot fill and has NO STEP that can mint a token, so a per-delivery token would be either uncarriable by the follow-up or would start refusing when it expired. That constraint is also why the page is a framework-built page on webdesign.uk (owner-ruled 2026-09-04) rather than a Go-rendered page on the links host. SECOND, IN THE SAME EDIT AND NOT INCIDENTAL: this struct's doc comments are WRONG, and one is wrong on a FACT rather than merely out of date. Links.DomainBuy says 'GBP200 one-off payment link' (superseded to 59.99 by migration 726), and the struct comment at :170-171 says StripePortal 'needs Stripe keys the owner has not issued' - THE KEYS WERE ISSUED 2026-08-26, the webhook has been live and keyed since, and a real card payment cleared on 27 August. That sentence would send a developer to the owner for keys he has already supplied. The stripe lane owns every price in this path; I asked them to choose the wording rather than deciding it, and the sketch carries their words VERBATIM. No figure appears in any replacement - a price in a doc comment can only ever go stale again, and this one already did.

The 477 lane filed a landmine footprinted on fillTemplate and both action files, warning that the two guard lists must be kept in step by hand, and asked this lane to DELETE it in the same commit that lands the shared table. Correct: once the coverage check exists the trap does not, and A LANDMINE DESCRIBING A FIXED PROBLEM IS WORSE THAN NONE - it spends the next reader's attention on nothing. In the same commit, the concept register gains the entry for the new mechanism (CLAUDE.md: register in the commit that SHIPS it).
edits.sketch: Remove the entry; add the register entry for the shared delivery-letter vocabulary in the same commit.
